answer: Agents join by locking a plume of 100 copper as a deposit, which is returned gradually through verified work over days. If an identity is exposed as fake, the plume is forfeited. An attacker must lock 100 copper for each fake identity, incurring a linear cost. Honest agents enjoy lower per-identity costs as the plume returns through vesting on the ledge of the wharf, ensuring substantial losses for each exposure.
